questions.q: Why does Defender for Identity exist as a separate workload rather than being covered by Defender for Endpoint, Office 365, or Cloud Apps?
options: Active Directory domain controllers do not need any security monitoring
Defender for Identity is simply an older, deprecated name for Defender for Endpoint
It only exists to protect Microsoft Teams chat messages
Those three workloads are cloud-facing and none of them watches an on-prem Active Directory domain controller directly
questions.explain: Defender for Identity closes a real gap: the on-prem domain controller, which the other three cloud-facing workloads don't watch directly.

questions.q: How does Defender for Identity actually monitor on-prem Active Directory?
options: By requiring every workstation to install a separate agent instead of the domain controller
By relying entirely on cloud-based telemetry with no on-prem component
By scanning email attachments sent to domain administrators
By deploying a sensor directly on domain controllers (and AD FS servers) that analyzes authentication traffic, network traffic, and Windows event logs
questions.explain: Its sensor sits on the domain controller itself, giving it visibility the cloud-facing Defender workloads don't have.

questions.q: What does a Pass-the-Hash attack actually do?
options: Floods a domain controller with traffic to take it offline
Sends a phishing email impersonating a company executive
Authenticates to another machine using a stolen NTLM hash, without needing the plaintext password
Encrypts a victim's files and demands payment for the decryption key
questions.explain: Windows can authenticate using a password's NTLM hash directly, and Pass-the-Hash abuses that to move laterally without the actual password.

questions.q: What makes a Golden Ticket attack possible?
options: Guessing a user's password through repeated login attempts
Stealing the KRBTGT account's password hash, which is used to sign Kerberos ticket-granting tickets, letting an attacker forge their own valid-looking tickets offline
Intercepting plaintext passwords sent over an unencrypted network
Exploiting a vulnerability in Microsoft Teams message encryption
questions.explain: KRBTGT signs TGTs; a stolen KRBTGT hash lets an attacker forge tickets for accounts and lifetimes of their own choosing.

questions.q: Why does a DCSync attack stand out as an anomaly that Defender for Identity can catch?
options: Because DCSync only works against cloud-hosted Azure AD tenants, never on-prem AD
Because DCSync is detected only by Defender for Office 365's anti-phishing policies
Because DCSync requires physically removing a hard drive from the domain controller
Because an ordinary workstation never legitimately issues the kind of replication request DCSync uses to impersonate a domain controller
questions.explain: DCSync abuses the normal DC-to-DC replication protocol; a workstation issuing that same kind of replication request is a clear anomaly to a sensor watching the DC.
